author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 우리나라 산림 전역에서 번식하는 흔한 텃새로, 낙엽활엽수림과 솔숲, 잡목림, 관목림 등에 살며 주로 나무 위에서 지낸다. 번식기에는 암수가 함께 다니고, 그 밖의 때에는 4~5마리나 10마리 남짓한 가족 무리를 이루며 때로 다른 종과 섞여 큰 무리가 된다. 숲속에 둥지를 틀고 4~6월에 한배에 7~11개, 때로는 13개의 알을 낳는다. 곤충을 주로 먹고 거미류와 콩과식물 씨앗도 먹으며, 한반도 전역과 유라시아 대륙에 분포한다.

art.subject: Long-tailed Tit (Aegithalos caudatus), adult (sexes alike, Korean form with a striped head): forehead, centre of the crown, cheeks, chin and throat white; a broad black band from above the eye running back along the side of the crown to the nape and mantle; mantle and back black; scapulars pinkish; wings blackish-brown with whitish edges to the tertials; underparts whitish with a pink wash on the flanks and vent; very long, narrow black tail with white outer edges; tiny stubby black bill; dark brown eye; dark brown legs with pale brown feathering on the thighs.
art.pose: perched on a thin twig high in a tree, one of a small family flock
art.scene: Korean deciduous broadleaf and pine woodland with shrubby undergrowth; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a thin twig: white head with a broad black band from above the eye to the nape, black back, pinkish scapulars, blackish wings with pale tertial edges, very long black tail edged white, tiny black bill
adult, front view perched on a twig: white face and throat, black bands framing the white crown, whitish breast, pinkish flanks, very long tail hanging below
art.build: Tiny round songbird, about 14cm, of which more than half is tail; the body is a fluffy ball smaller than a Marsh Tit's. Round head, no visible neck. Bill very short, stubby and triangular, black. Legs short, dark brown. Wings short and rounded; at rest the wingtips reach only the base of the tail. Tail very long, narrow and graduated, longer than the body. Travels in chattering family flocks through the canopy, often hanging upside down.
avoid: Do not paint a pure white head without black bands; that is the northern race, not the Korean birds.
Do not paint a long thin bill; the bill is a tiny stub.
Do not shorten the tail; it is longer than the body.
Do not paint a rufous crown and brown body; that is Vinous-throated Parrotbill.
